pubchem.title: Valencene
pubchem.description: (+)-valencene is a carbobicyclic compound and sesquiterpene that is 1,2,3,4,4a,5,6,7-octahydronaphthalene which is substituted a prop-1-en-2-yl group at position 3 and by methyl groups at positions 4a and 5 (the 3R,4aS,5R- diastereoisomer). It is a sesquiterpene, a polycyclic olefin and a carbobicyclic compound.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: (+)-Valencene is a sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule responsible for the bright, sweet, and woody aromas of certain citrus fruits. It is widely used as a fragrance and flavor ingredient, giving a characteristic citrusy lift to everyday foods, drinks, and perfumes.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is famously abundant in citrus fruits, particularly sweet oranges (Citrus sinensis), bitter oranges (Citrus aurantium), and grapefruits (Citrus paradisi). It can also be found in aromatic herbs like Artemisia and the American beautyberry (Callicarpa americana).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are fascinated by valencene not just for its own bright scent, but because it is a crucial stepping stone to producing nootkatone, one of the most sought-after and expensive grapefruit aromatic compounds. Because extracting it from citrus is costly, scientists are heavily focused on metabolic engineering, using yeasts like Saccharomyces cerevisiae to brew valencene sustainably. Beyond its industrial appeal, researchers are exploring its biological potential, with the strongest evidence currently resting on human observational studies (Oxford level 2b) looking at its antioxidant and insect-repelling properties.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether valencene interacts with cellular pathways, including cytochrome P450 enzymes, to influence cell health and proliferation.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial (Oxford 1b) supplementing valencene in a high-risk cohort, measuring specific biomarkers of cellular proliferation and oxidative stress over six months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early observational and lab work points toward valencene having protective properties against certain microbes, raising questions about its role in food preservation or skin defense.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind human topical trial (Oxford 1b) applying a valencene-based formulation versus placebo to measure changes in skin microbiome composition and bacterial load over four weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: If early animal findings bear out, valencene might interact with neurological pathways to support cognitive clarity and memory retention.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A first-in-human randomized controlled trial (Oxford 1b) giving a standardized valencene dose to healthy adults and measuring cognitive performance and memory recall using standardized computer tasks over a 12-week period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether valencene can modulate inflammatory pathways, potentially offering a natural way to support tissue recovery and comfort.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial (Oxford 1b) measuring systemic inflammatory markers (like CRP and cytokines) in healthy adults given a daily valencene supplement for eight weeks.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) for its antioxidant and insect-repelling properties, while much of the remaining research consists of animal studies and metabolic engineering research.
